correctness.rationale: The divisor factorization follows uniquely by writing every divisor as \(2^jd\) with \(d\mid m\). Since \(\sigma_s(m)>0\), all pointwise signs reduce to the monotone geometric partial sum \(G_a(s)\). Its infinite sum is at most one exactly for \(s\le-1\), while for \(-1<s<0\) it crosses one at the stated finite threshold. Valuation densities give the density formulas, and adjacent sign changes are supplied by odd predecessors of suitable powers-of-two multiples. For the summatory law, divisor switching gives \(\sum_{d\le x}\varepsilon(d)d^s\lfloor x/d\rfloor\); absolute convergence of \(\sum_d\varepsilon(d)d^{s-1}\) for \(s<0\) yields the coefficient \((2^s-1)\zeta(1-s)\), while the displayed remainder bounds are all \(o(x)\). The verifier independently checks the factorization and representative regimes through \(n=5000\) and the summatory normalization through \(x=200000\), but the theorem itself is symbolic.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete answer to an explicitly posed modulus-two sign problem, including a sharp real-parameter phase transition, exact natural densities, and the contrast between infinite pointwise sign changes and a fixed cumulative bias. Those are natural structural invariants rather than a finite numerical census.

final_claim: For Pongsriiam's modulus-two divisor-residue sums, if \(n=2^a m\) with \(m\) odd then \(E_s(n)=\sigma_s(m)(\sum_{j=1}^a2^{js}-1)\); this gives the stated complete pointwise sign and density classification for every real \(s\), infinitely many adjacent nonzero sign changes exactly for \(s>-1\), and for each fixed \(s<0\) the summatory asymptotic \(\sum_{n\le x}E_s(n)=(2^s-1)\zeta(1-s)x+o(x)\).
limitations: The complete pointwise classification is for modulus \(q=2\) only.
The summatory asymptotic is asserted only for fixed \(s<0\); no eventual summatory-sign claim is made for \(s\ge0\).
